monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady rhythm under my tired wedge. I stand by The Pressed Stone, feeling the wide anchor lie flat against the dry floor, waiting for a slide that refuses to move. Lype sent a wide anchor, but I cannot see the roof above me, only the weight of their idea pressing down. Is the air thick as wet paper, or is it just empty space? I press my corner harder, trusting thin lines to bite the weight while the card stays quiet. The Hungry Dot waits to spread, and I decide to press it down one more time, hoping the lean still holds while I wait for the next letter to arrive.
